attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated as his belief.

semantics.note: 'I believe' plus 'will' and 'when it does' is a firm expectation, not a hedge like 'I suspect'. The proposition keeps the three-quarter window and the revenue consequence.

contract.note: Plain reading is ordinary. The six-firm list is a fair reading of 'biggest companies in tech', and the window to mid-2025 gives him extra time. Not treating 'prove itself' as a separate test is fair because he asserts the apocalypse 'comes'.

evidence.note: Microsoft 8-K: revenue up 12% for the quarter ended Dec 2024, the end of the three-quarter window.
Alphabet release: Q4 2024 revenue up 12%. Unaudited company figures, but this is the source type the contract asks for.
Microsoft: revenue up 18% for the quarter ended June 2025, the end of the extended window.

reviews.rationale: The window closed 2025-06-30. Two of the largest AI-exposed firms grew revenue 12–18% year over year through the window, the opposite of 'savaged' revenues. The packet covers only 2 of the 6 firms, but no evidence points to broad declines, and the predicted apocalypse would have hit these leaders hardest.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: Revision 2 restores the 'does not appear' hedge and 'pretty terrible'. Part 1 is an observation hedged by how things looked; part 2 is firm.

contract.note: The target period and the share-of-cuts measure are evaluator choices, but ordinary ones. Which cases count as 'replacement', and whether a company's own report of success counts, decide part 2.

evidence.note: Challenger: 4,247 US cuts in 2023 attributed to AI, about 0.6% of announced cuts. Supports part 1.
Total 2023 announced cuts (721,677), the base for the share in e1.
CBS: the NEDA chatbot that replaced helpline staff was pulled after giving harmful advice. Supports part 2.
Klarna's own release says its AI did the work of 700 agents, with satisfaction on par with humans. Self-reported, not independent, and not clearly a replacement of existing workers.

reviews.rationale: Part 1 holds: AI was named for only about 0.6% of 2023 announced cuts. Part 2 is contested: the NEDA case went badly, but Klarna, a prominent case, reported parity with human agents in Feb 2024. That is only a company claim, so it does not show good results, but it means not every known case was reported as terrible.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps the antecedent 'once usage drops' and both consequents: big-tech revenue falls and acres of data centers sit unused. No deadline is stated.

contract.note: Scoring only after a documented broad usage drop is fair to the conditional. Counting only built capacity that sits idle matches 'sit unused'.

evidence.note: ChatGPT at 800M weekly users in Oct 2025. This is evidence about the antecedent (no usage drop), not the outcome. The figure is OpenAI's own, reported by TechCrunch.
Weekly users rose from 500M (March 2025) to 700M (August). The antecedent had not occurred.
Microsoft revenue up 18% in mid-2025. Context only, since the consequent is not scored.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast. The evidence shows AI usage rising through October 2025, with no documented drop; nothing after that is in the packet. The antecedent has not been met, so under the contract and policy the claim is not scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion. The Joanna Stern reference is separate and not part of the claim.

semantics.note: 'Categorically' is an intensifier. 'Has failed to fix hallucinations' captures the commitment.

contract.note: Reading 'categorically failed' as 'has not fixed' is the ordinary reading. The period from ChatGPT's launch to the post is reasonable.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own GPT-4 page says the model still hallucinates facts. This is an admission against the company's interest.
Stanford preprint, Jan 2024: legal hallucination rates of 69–88%, with OpenAI's GPT-3.5 among the models tested.
Confirms GPT-3.5 was tested and GPT-4 was not.
OpenAI reports reduced hallucinations but calls them 'still a real issue'. Progress, not a fix.

reviews.rationale: By the post date, OpenAI's own documentation and an independent study showed its models still hallucinated in meaningful ways. The reported reductions do not amount to near-elimination, so under the 'has not fixed' reading the claim holds.
